editorial:
Imagine being thousands of feet up a snowy mountain in Peru with your best friend, only for everything to go wrong in a split second. You get a front-row seat to the nightmare Joe Simpson and Simon Yates face during their 1985 climb of Siula Grande. The vibe is super tense from the start because you know they are in over their heads. It feels less like a boring history lesson and more like a survival thriller that keeps you on the edge of your seat. You really feel the bond between the two climbers and the panic that sets in when an injury turns their dream trip into a fight for their lives.

What makes this work is how it mixes real interviews with dramatic recreations that look incredibly real. The pacing is great, and the moral dilemma about whether to cut a rope is something you will be thinking about long after the credits roll. If you love stories about human will, you need to see this. To get the most out of the stunning mountain views, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a smart move.
endingExplained: After a brutal crawl across the rocks with a broken leg, Joe finally reaches the base camp. The big shock is that he finds Simon already there. Simon had to cut the rope to save himself, believing Joe was already dead. They are both shocked to see each other alive. The movie ends with them talking about the trauma and how they moved past the guilt and anger to remain friends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true survival stories and mountain climbing.
